headline: LinkedUp Users Discover Profiles With Job Histories From the Future
subheadline: At least 847 accounts list employment dates extending to 2030 and beyond
summary: A glitch—or something else—has revealed LinkedUp profiles showing work experience at companies that don't exist yet, for dates years in the future.
content:
It started with a connection request from someone whose profile listed their current job as starting in 2027.

LinkedUp user @RecruitingReal noticed the anomaly while reviewing connection requests and posted a screenshot to Threadit. The profile showed a complete work history—but the dates were wrong. The person's "current role" began in 2027. Their previous job ended in 2026. The education dates were normal.

"I figured it was a typo," @RecruitingReal wrote. "Then I checked the company. It doesn't exist. But the profile has recommendations from coworkers. Coworkers whose profiles also show jobs at companies that don't exist, with dates in the future."

The community has since identified 847 profiles with future-dated employment histories. The profiles are otherwise normal—photos that reverse-image-search to no other sources, connection networks, activity histories, skill endorsements. But the jobs don't match reality.

Patterns include:

- Most "future" jobs are at companies containing the words "Quantum," "Omni," or "Integrated"
- Multiple profiles list employment at "Omnicorp Holdings" starting in 2028
- One profile shows a position at "Hartwell Building Management" beginning 2031, listing Mars (of The Underground) as a reference
- 47 profiles list job titles containing the word "Coordinator" with no further description

"The weirdest part is the recommendations," noted u/FutureHR. "Real recommendations from people with normal profiles, talking about working with these people at companies that don't exist on projects that haven't happened. Either someone is running the most elaborate fake-profile scheme ever, or these people have genuinely worked together somewhere we can't see."

LinkedUp's trust and safety team issued a statement: "We are investigating a small number of profiles with data integrity issues. These profiles appear to have been affected by a database error. We are working to correct the affected records."

The statement did not explain how a database error could generate coherent fake companies, fake recommendations, and employment dates in the future.

Derek attempted to connect with one of the future-dated profiles to ask questions. His connection request was accepted within seconds—at 3:47 AM. The profile owner's only message: "You'll understand when you get here."

The community has compiled a list of the future companies mentioned across the profiles. Most are generic tech startups. But one appears on 47 profiles: "Hartwell Temporal Solutions, LLC."

No record of this company exists in any corporate database. At press time, @RecruitingReal received another connection request from 2028.
author: Marcus Webb, Internet Culture Correspondent
